entry.title: The $RO(C_2)$-graded Hurewicz image of Atiyah's Real K-theory
entry.summary: author: Zhouli Xu; abstract: stable stems
entry.content:
author: Zhouli Xu; abstract: stable stems

Sihao Ma, Xiaolin Danny Shi, Zhouli Xu, Albert Jinghui Yang, Shangjie Zhang

We determine the $RO(C_2)$-graded $k\mathbb R$-Hurewicz image, where $k \mathbb R$ denotes the connective Atiyah's Real $K$-theory spectrum. As a consequence, we obtain four infinite families in the $RO(C_2)$-graded equivariant stable stems that are $C_2$-equivariant refinements of the classical $\mu$-families. Using a $C_2$-equivariant $v_{1,0}$-self map, we explicitly construct an equivariant Adams periodicity operator $P_{C_2}$ that captures these $v_1$-periodicity phenomena in the $C_2$-stable stems.

entry.title: A prismatic Riemann-Hilbert correspondence
entry.content:
title: prismatic

Dylan Pentland

We study the category of constructible $p$-Kummer-\'{e}tale sheaves on the log adic generic fiber $(\mathrm{X},\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{D}})_\eta$ for the stratification induced by a horizontal normal crossings divisor $\mathrm{D}$, showing that it is antiequivalent to a category of finitely generated unit Laurent crystals on the log prismatic site. We give a local description of finitely generated unit crystals on a framed log affine in terms of $(\varphi,\Gamma)$-modules, and show pushforward compatibility for strict log smooth proper morphisms.

entry.title: The classical homotopy category is cartesian closed
entry.content:
abstract: (infinity, 1)

Zhen Lin Low

The category of all topological spaces and homotopy classes of maps is cartesian closed. In fact, the $(\infty, 1)$-category of all topological spaces and continuous maps, localised at homotopy equivalences, is cartesian closed. We model the exponential object using a topological space whose points are continuous maps equipped with putative neighbourhood filters. In general, this topological space will not even be $T_1$-separated, but the evaluation map induces a natural weak homotopy equivalence witnessing the universal property.

entry.title: $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth approximation of mod $k$ integral cycles
entry.content:
Gianmarco Caldini, Anna Skorobogatova

We prove that every mod $k$ integral cycle $T$ of sufficiently high codimension in an oriented Riemannian manifold $\mathcal{M}$ can be approximated in flat norm by a cycle which is a $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth submanifold $\Sigma$ of nearly the same area, up to a singular set of codimension 5. If in addition $T$ belongs to a mod $k$ homology class admitting an embedded $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth manifold representative, then $\Sigma$ can be taken fully regular, up to the codimension one stratum of classical singularities. This extends the smooth approximation theory to cycles with coefficients in $\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$ in stable regimes. Moreover, we provide examples showing the impossibility of locally approximating minimizing cycles by smooth or $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth submanifolds, even in homology classes with smooth or $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth representatives.

entry.title: Anomalies, higher symmetries, and homotopy theory I: crossed precosheaves and a nonabelian Cech construction
entry.content:
Anton Kapustin, Shixiong Xu

Symmetries of a quantum field theory or a quantum lattice model are expected to be described not by a group but by a homotopy type, whose homotopy groups are the higher symmetry groups and whose Postnikov invariants encode 't Hooft anomalies. We propose a homotopy-theoretic definition of 't Hooft anomalies based on the structure of localized symmetries in the operator-algebraic approach. The input is a crossed precosheaf: a collection of groups attached to regions of space, equipped with pairings recording that the commutator of two transformations localized in two regions is localized in their intersection. To a crossed precosheaf and a finite family of regions we attach a pointed connected homotopy type, the Cech-Loday classifying space. As the family of regions ranges over finite covers of space, the classifying spaces form a pro-object in the homotopy category. There is a canonical map from the ordinary classifying space of the symmetry group to this pro-type. Composing this map with a group action gives an anomaly whose nontriviality obstructs gauging. In favorable cases, the Cech-Loday space is essentially independent of the cover. In such cases, the homotopy fiber of the canonical map is a candidate for the classifying space of the higher group of symmetries. We give examples of crossed precosheaves arising from gauge transformations in continuum field theory and from quantum cellular automata and finite-depth circuits. For quantum spin systems in one and two dimensions, our construction recovers the Else-Nayak index and its generalizations to two dimensions.

entry.title: Discrete Morse Theory for Computing Filtered Cosheaf Homology
entry.content:
Neria Baris

This paper addresses the computation of persistent homology for filtrations of cellular cosheaves over a fixed cell complex, where the algebraic data vary along the filtration while the underlying topological structure remains unchanged. We extend methods from discrete Morse theory to this setting, establishing conditions under which chain complexes can be reduced while preserving the associated persistence module. Building on these results, we introduce "FilteredScythe", an algorithm that identifies Morse matchings compatible with all stages of the filtration and performs reductions using Schur complements, based on the exist "Scythe" algorithm. We prove the correctness of these reductions and establish bounds on the algorithm's time and space complexity.

entry.title: On the work of Graeme Segal
entry.content:
Daniel S. Freed

This is my written Laudatio for Graeme Segal on receiving the Chern Medal at the 2026 International Congress of Mathematicians. I make some general remarks about Segal's qualities as a mathematician. Then I discuss the origins of his work on classifying spaces of categories and Gamma-spaces. In the last section I describe his axiom system for Wick-rotated quantum field theory and some of his subsequent work in the area. Of course, this is necessarily only a small slice of Segal's total research output.

entry.title: Real Tree Vineyards have Vines
entry.content:
Michael Hull, Thomas Payne, Thomas Weighill

We show that every vineyard can be decomposed into vines, that is, every path in the space of persistence diagrams $\mathcal{D}$ can be decomposed into a sequence of paths in $\mathbb R^2$. Moreover, we characterize which spaces $X$ have the property that every continuous map $X\to \mathcal{D}$ has such a decomposition. Our results hold not just for $\mathcal{D}$, but also for many other spaces of unordered tuples.

entry.title: Equivariant generating hypotheses for finite groups
entry.summary: author: Zhouli Xu; title: equivariant; abstract: g-spectr
entry.content:
author: Zhouli Xu; title: equivariant; abstract: g-spectr

Sihao Ma, XiaoLin Danny Shi, Zhouli Xu, Shangjie Zhang

We prove that no nontrivial finite group $G$ satisfies the equivariant generating hypothesis of Bohmann, even when all $RO(H)$-graded homotopy groups are tested for every subgroup $H\leq G$. For each $G$, we construct ghosts on finite $G$-spectra with arbitrarily long nonzero composition powers. We also prove that the homotopy-module functors are nonfull and construct non-equivalent finite $G$-spectra with isomorphic full homotopy modules. A central ingredient of our proof is the natural ghost operation $\Psi=(p-[C_p/e])(1-g)$ on $C_p$-spectra. Motivated by Ma--Xu's examples in the motivic settings, we apply this operation to both a two-cell complex and products of complex projective spaces with cyclic permutation action, which produces arbitrarily long nonzero ghost powers. We also construct a ghost on an explicit four-cell complex that is detected in the derived category over the group ring.

entry.title: Straightening for lax transformations and adjunctions of $(\infty,2)$-categories
entry.summary: author (watch): Fernando Abellán; author (watch): Andrea Gagna; author: Rune Haugseng; title: (infinity,2); title: straightening
entry.content:
author (watch): Fernando Abellán; author (watch): Andrea Gagna; author: Rune Haugseng; title: (infinity,2); title: straightening

Fernando Abell\'an, Andrea Gagna, Rune Haugseng

We prove an unstraightening result for lax transformations between functors from an arbitrary $(\infty,2)$-category to that of $(\infty,2)$-categories. We apply this to study partially (op)lax and weighted (co)limits, giving fibrational descriptions of such (co)limits for diagrams valued in $(\infty,2)$-categories, to characterize adjoints in $(\infty,2)$-categories of functors and (op)lax transformations, and to prove a mate correspondence between lax transformations that are componentwise right adjoints and oplax transformations that are componentwise left adjoints, for such transformations among functors between arbitrary $(\infty,2)$-categories.

entry.title: A characterization of central extensions relative to n-nilpotent objects
entry.content:
title: nilpoten

Marino Gran, James R. A. Gray

We characterize the central extensions, in the sense of the categorical theory of central extensions of Janelidze and Kelly, relative to the Birkhoff subcategory of $n$-nilpotent objects of a semi-abelian and algebraically coherent category. An extension $f \colon A \to B$ with kernel $K$ turns out to be central precisely when the iterated Huq commutator $[A,[A,\dots,[A,K]\dots]]$, with $n$ occurrences of $A$, vanishes. For $n=2$ this condition reads $[A,[K,A]] = 0$, that is, $[K,A]$ is a central subobject of $A$. In the special case of groups this description was obtained by Everaert and the first author. The present proof is categorical, and applies in particular to Lie algebras, to crossed modules, to cocommutative Hopf algebras over a field, and to any category of interest.

entry.title: Integral trace duality and the Witt filtration on Lubin--Tate space
entry.content:
title: lubin-tate

Andrea Taccani

Let $\mathcal O$ be the Lubin--Tate deformation ring of a one-dimensional commutative formal group of finite height $n\geq1$ over a perfect field $k$ of characteristic $p$. We identify Rezk's Witt filtration $\{I_d\}$ with the divisibility filtration of integral trace pairings on subgroup algebras of fixed source lifts. This gives the geometric recursion \[ I_{d+1}=pI_d+J_{d,z}\qquad(d\geq0), \] where $J_{d,z}$ defines the targets of order-$p^d$ quotient isogenies from a $W(k)$-valued lift $z$ of the closed point. The corrected ideal is independent of $z$. We also compute the cokernel of the universal source trace pairing over $\mathcal O$: it is $\bigoplus_{j=1}^d(\mathcal O/p^j)^{r_j-r_{j-1}}$, where $r_j$ counts order-$p^j$ subgroups of $(\mathbf Q_p/\mathbf Z_p)^n$. The same duality extends the generic trace along two-step isogeny flags to an integral surjection, even when the flag-forgetting map is not flat. This computes composition in the subring of weighted trace operations. Applications include sharp projector denominators and congruence fibre products for full-torsion loci.

entry.title: Models for dagger $(\infty,1)$-categories III: Univalent flagged dagger $(\infty,1)$-categories and unitarily complete dagger Segal anima
entry.content:
title: (infinity,1)

Keima Akasaka

We identify the $(\infty,1)$-category presented by the dagger Bergner, dagger Joyal, and dagger Rezk models of Parts I and II with that of univalent flagged dagger $(\infty,1)$-categories. We first construct a realization--nerve adjunction between reversal simplicial anima and Hermitian flags. We prove that its nerve restricts to an equivalence between flagged dagger $(\infty,1)$-categories and dagger Segal anima, under which univalence corresponds to unitary completeness. We then construct the adjunctions for univalentization and Hermitian completion and identify univalentization with unitary completion.

entry.title: Generalized Thom Spectra, Conjugate Stacks, and truncated Brown-Peterson Spectra
entry.content:
abstract: topological hochschild homology

Preston Cranford

We propose a of definition conjugate stack for a class of suitable $\mathbb{E}_3$-$\mathrm{MU}$-algebras that includes the truncated Brown-Peterson spectra $\mathrm{BP}\langle n \rangle$ for all heights $n$. Then we calculate part of $\mathrm{BP}\langle n \rangle^{\mathrm{conj}}$ as a quotient stack in terms of Witt vectors. To perform this computation we study generalized Thom spectra and their relative Topological Hochschild Homology. We exhibit the Eilenberg-Mac Lane spectrum $\mathrm{H}\mathbb{F}_2$ as a $\mathbb{E}_3$-$\mathrm{MU}$-Thom spectrum, the $p$-local Eilenberg-Mac Lane spectra $\mathrm{H}\mathbb{Z}/p^n$ (except for $\mathrm{H}\mathbb{Z}/4$) and $\mathrm{H}\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$ as $\mathbb{E}_3$-$\mathrm{MU}_{(p)}$-Thom spectra, and the connective complex K-theory spectrum $ku$ as $\mathbb{E}_1$-$\mathrm{MU}$-Thom spectra. We accompany these ``go" results with ``no-go" results that show these ``go" results do not admit $\mathbb{E}_{\infty}$-refinements.

entry.title: The Becker-Gottlieb transfer is not functorial: An example using $C_\infty$-algebras
entry.content:
abstract: thh

Florian Naef, Robin Stoll

We prove that the Becker-Gottlieb transfer is not functorial, even on rational cohomology. More precisely, for any even $n \ge 4$, we construct a fibration $f \colon X \to S^{n+1}$ with fiber $S^2 \vee S^n$, and an oriented $S^1$-bundle $g \colon Y \to X$ such that the transfer of $f \circ g$ is non-trivial on rational cohomology. Since the transfer of an oriented $S^1$-bundle vanishes, this implies that the transfer of $f \circ g$ and the composite of the transfers of $f$ and $g$ induce different maps on rational cohomology and are thus not homotopic. The proof that the transfer of $f \circ g$ is non-trivial uses the rational models for the Becker--Gottlieb and THH transfers obtained in previous work of the authors. In the appendix, we provide a second, more involved, proof that relies on constructing explicit $C_\infty$-algebra models for odd spherical fibrations (including circle bundles), which might be of independent interest. Concurrently, another counterexample (of very different flavor) was found by Georg Lehner, Cary Malkiewich, and the first author.

entry.title: Curvature, diameter and bounded Betti numbers
entry.content:
Zhongmin Shen, Jyh-Yang Wu

We consider the image of the comparison homomorphism from bounded cohomology to ordinary cohomology. Its dimension is called the bounded Betti number. In our earlier work we proved that the total bounded Betti number of a closed Riemannian $n$-manifold satisfying $\Ric\geq -(n-1)$ and $\Diam\leq D$ is bounded by a constant depending only on $n$ and $D$. The original proof used the amenability of the images of sufficiently small local fundamental groups. Since that work was written, Kapovitch and Wilking proved Gromov's generalized Margulis lemma under a lower Ricci curvature bound. Their theorem gives the stronger conclusion that these local groups are uniformly virtually nilpotent. We explain how their result supplies a direct modern input for the bounded Betti number theorem. We also discuss the topological meaning of the bounded part of ordinary cohomology and its relation to the $\ell^1$-seminorm on homology.

entry.title: Cyclic reflections and the flip equation for the graded Grothendieck-Teichm\"uller group
entry.content:
Chandan Singh

Furusho, Hirose and Komiyama reformulated the pentagon equation using an involution called the flip, which led to a new characterisation of the graded Grothendieck-Teichm\"uller group $\mathsf{GRT}_1$. We show that the flip is a reflection in the cyclic structure of the operad of framed Drinfeld-Kohno Lie algebras, with the framings removed. Applying the reflection twice to the pentagon gives the two-cycle relation for every Drinfeld associator. This relation is precisely the condition for cyclic compatibility on the associativity morphism, giving a new proof that $\mathsf{GRT}_1$ acts by cyclic automorphisms of parenthesized ribbon chord diagrams.

entry.title: Exact Topological Compliance: Generating Persistence-Equivalent Graphs
entry.content:
Mattie Ji, Indradyumna Roy, Vikas Garg

Persistent homology summarizes the topological evolution of a graph as persistence diagrams (PDs). Generating graphs whose topology matches a target descriptor is increasingly important, yet existing topology-aware generative models rely on soft regularization, producing graphs whose PDs may only be approximately similar. We initiate a principled investigation of the generation problem: produce graphs that realize a target PD exactly. We propose two approaches guided by the implicit local and global constraints a target PD imposes. The local approach builds degree-based PD-equivalent graphs iteratively, and we prove that every output realizes the target PD and that every degree-based PD-equivalent graph is reachable. However, as shown thereafter, local generation necessarily trades off between sample diversity and reaching infeasible states. We therefore recast generation as a global constraint satisfaction problem with a complete encoding solvable by modern constraint programming solvers. This is applicable to any vertex-based permutation equivariant filtration scheme and is minimal under the degree filtration. Experiments on four standard graph generation benchmarks confirm that both methods realize the target PD exactly. Together, our methods provide a principled treatment of strict topology-compliant graph generation. Code is available at https://github.com/Aalto-QuML/ExactCompliance.

entry.title: Groups with the fixed-point property
entry.content:
Nicolas Monod, Omer Tamuz, Lizzy Teryoshin

We propose the study of the class of groups that fix a point for every continuous action on any convex compact space. Oliver completed the corresponding program of classifying the finite groups that have this fixed-point property in finite dimensions. Turning to infinite groups, the Schauder--Tychonoff theorem establishes that the integers have the fixed-point property, but this has not been shown for any other infinite, finitely generated group. We establish a local transfer principle and use it to show, as a proof of concept, that $\mathbf{Z} \times (\mathbf{Z}/p\mathbf{Z})$ belongs to this class of groups.

Georg Lehner, Cary Malkiewich, Florian Naef

We show by explicit counterexample that the Becker--Gottlieb transfer cannot be made functorial. A different counterexample using rational homotopy theory was discovered concurrently by the third author and Robin Stoll.

entry.title: The rational homology of independence complexes of Kneser graphs on triples
entry.content:
Ziqin Feng

The independence complex of the Kneser graph $\KG(n,k)$ is the simplicial complex of pairwise intersecting families of $n$-subsets of $[2n+k]$; equivalently, it is a Vietoris--Rips complex of the $n$-subsets of $[2n+k]$ under the symmetric-difference metric. Feng and Wang asked whether, for $n=3$, its reduced homology is nontrivial only in dimensions $6$ and $9$, and conjectured the rank in dimension $9$. We answer the question affirmatively over the rationals and determine all the associated Betti numbers. For every $k\ge0$, the only nonzero reduced Betti numbers using rationals of $\Ind(\KG(3,k))$ are \[ \beta_6=\binom{k+5}{7}+29\binom{k+6}{7} \qquad\text{and}\qquad \beta_9=\binom{k+6}{6}. \] The proof uses an inductive decomposition based on a simplicial retraction and Barmak's star clusters, Dowker duality together with Jonsson's computation of the homology of complexes of graphs with bounded covering number, and a relative Mayer--Vietoris spectral sequence which reduces the problem to the six-element sets.

entry.title: A Note on Laminar Presentations and Finite Chain Models for Ample Groupoid Homology
entry.content:
Luciano Melodia

A finite free chain model for the homology of a Hausdorff ample groupoid \(G\) is cut out of the Matui complex by a finite clopen partition of each nerve space. We ask what such a model must supply and isolate three requirements: a single model that is a quasi-isomorphism, a chain of models that is a complete system with ranks and transition maps read off the presenting data, and a bound on the number of atoms in terms of the presenting cover. An \(n\)-Helly axiom on the presenting covers supplies none of them, being satisfied by every finite atomization for every \(n\), and a \(1\)-Helly family of \(N\) compact open sets can have \(2^{N}-1\) atoms. We show that a laminar presentation, a laminar basis of compact open sets in each nerve degree, supplies the third, and the second as soon as it is countable: the atoms of a finite laminar family are exactly its nonempty nodes, so a subordinate model has rank at most the number of members presenting it, the subordinate models of finite height form a complete system containing, for a countable presentation, a chain that is itself complete, and the transition maps are the least-ancestor maps of the presenting subfamilies. Every second countable Hausdorff ample groupoid admits one, and the choice is made in each nerve degree separately, laminarity not being stable under products. The first requirement is a restriction on \(G\): the homology of a model is finitely generated over a Noetherian ring, whereas \(H_0\) over \(\mathbb Z\) is not for the unit groupoid on a Cantor set or for the CAR groupoid, and a truncated model carries free homology of arbitrary rank in arbitrarily high odd degree where the groupoid has none. The chain-level statements are accompanied by a Lean 4 formalization.

entry.title: Axiomatic degree theory on topological manifolds
entry.content:
Stoyan Apostolov

In this note we study extension of standard Euclidean degree in nonlinear analysis to the setting of general oriented topological manifolds. The axiomatization of Euclidean degree is adapted to this setting. Existence and uniqueness are proven. The existence does not rely on smooth approximations as in the Euclidean case -- this is irrelevant for manifolds which do not admit a smooth structure and could be ambiguous for manifolds admitting many smooth structures. Rather, we rely on a cohomological approach using only topological information. When compared to the Euclidean case, we think this approach makes the proofs simpler and more transparent. The standard notion of a degree of maps between closed oriented manifolds studied in algebraic topology is recovered as a special case. A generalization of the notion of winding number is developed and related to the notion of degree. The familiar composition formula of the Euclidean degree is also obtained in this context.

entry.title: Derived plethystic algebra
entry.content:
author: Benjamin Antieau; abstract: infinity-categor

Benjamin Antieau, Edith H\"ubner, Dmitry Kubrak, Joost Nuiten

We prove comparison results about $\infty$-categories of derived commutative rings with extra algebraic structure. For example, we show that several notions of derived $\delta$-rings agree and obtain similar results for derived $\lambda$-rings, derived binomial rings, and derived Boolean rings. Our comparison results apply more generally to modules over a specific kind of monad on derived rings that we call derived plethory.

entry.title: Quillen's local parameter conjecture in dimension four
entry.summary: abstract: motivic cohomolog; abstract: algebraic k-theor
entry.content:
abstract: motivic cohomolog; abstract: algebraic k-theor

Yunpeng Li

Let $R$ be a Noetherian regular local ring of mixed characteristic and dimension four, and let $r$ be a member of a regular system of parameters. We prove that every finitely generated projective module over $R[1/r]$ is free. We also prove that $\mathrm{Sp}_4(R[1/r])$ acts transitively on unimodular columns of length four and that every determinant orientation of a rank-two projective module is induced by a basis. The argument reduces freeness to two vanishing results: the degree-three Zariski cohomology of the naive degree-four Milnor--Witt sheaf and the alternating Witt group of $R[1/r]$. We establish these results using integral degree-two algebraic $K$-theory, supported hermitian $K$-theory, and local motivic cohomology. A finite-rank symplectic comparison relates the image of the completion obstruction to Milnor--Witt multiplication and yields the required symplectic frames.

entry.title: Reconstruction of graphs and surfaces from derived categories
entry.content:
abstract: infinity-categor; abstract: dualizable categor

Oscar Harr

A pair of topological spaces $X$ and $Y$ is a \emph{Fourier--Mukai (FM) pair} if there is an equivalence of $\infty$-categories of derived sheaves of abelian groups \[\operatorname{Shv}(X;\mathrm D(\mathbb Z))\simeq \operatorname{Shv}(Y;\mathrm D(\mathbb Z)).\] An FM pair $(X,Y)$ is \emph{non-trivial} if $X$ and $Y$ are not homeomorphic. We consider the question of whether non-trivial FM pairs $(X,Y)$ exist for which $X$ and $Y$ are both "nice" spaces, which in this article means admitting a triangulation. We show that the answer is no if $X$ is second-countable and either (i) one-dimensional, (ii) a surface, or (iii) the 3-sphere. In order to prove this, we define two invariants of dualizable categories. The first invariant is an extension of \emph{Tate--Hochschild cohomology} (aka singular Hochschild cohomology) to a class of dualizable categories satisfying a countability assumption. For a homology manifold $X$, we relate the Tate--Hochschild cohomology of $\operatorname{Shv}(X;\mathrm D(\mathbb Z))$ to the homology at infinity of $X$ (in the sense of proper homotopy theory). The second invariant takes the form of a subcategory $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{Gor}}\subseteq\mathcal D$ called the \emph{Gorenstein locus}, defined for every dualizable stable category $\mathcal D$. For a triangularizable space $X$ and a field $k$, we show that the Gorenstein locus of $\operatorname{Shv}(X;\mathrm D(k))$ is equal to the full subcategory of sheaves supported on the $k$-homology manifold locus of $X$.

entry.title: Constructive Bounds for the Topological Expressivity of Neural Networks
entry.content:
Kosio Beshkov

The expressivity of a neural network $\Phi$ describes the class of functions that a network can express. The term topological expressivity refers to a family of measures particularly suited to understand binary classification and is often formulated in terms of the Betti numbers of a decision boundary $\beta (\Phi^{-1}(0))$. Despite its popularity, this measure is not as useful for regression and other problems that do not involve a decision boundary. Instead, we propose to study topological expressivity in terms of the Betti numbers of the output of a neural network $\beta(\Phi(X))$. We formally prove that a ReLU network with architecture $(d,\sum\limits_{k=1}^{d } \beta_k(3k+2),\sum\limits_{k=1}^{d}\beta_k(k+1))$ can express spaces homotopy equivalent to wedge sums of spheres with arbitrary Betti numbers. This gives upper bounds for any arbitrary connected ($\beta_0=1$) sequence of Betti numbers, but by constructing spaces homotopy equivalent to products of $N$ spheres of dimension $d_1,...,d_N$ we achieve much better bounds $(\sum\limits_{n=1} d_n, 3\sum\limits_{n=1}\limits^N d_n + 2N, \sum\limits_{n=1}\limits^N d_n + N) $ for Betti numbers given by $\prod_n (1+x^{d_n})$. Finally we conjecture a much stronger tight bound which gives the architectural bound $(d,d+1,d+1)$ for a space homeomorphic to the sphere.

entry.title: Critical Point Theory for the Distance Function on PL-Spaces
entry.content:
Dirk Siersma

We study the (typical) singularities of the distance function from a point in the ambient space to a polytopal complex in Euclidean space. By means of the Goresky-MacPherson splitting we generalize the existing linear theory to the quadratic distance function. Critical points occur on `selected' strata of the PL-space, where normal Morse Data determine the change of topology. On the homology level there exist indices with multiplicities, combined in a Morse vector. We focus mainly on PL-manifolds. We give bounds, depending on the dimension of the strata. In low dimensions we describe singularity types. At the end we discuss relations with Discrete Morse Theory.

entry.title: The (right) homotopy between two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms
entry.content:
Mattia Ornaghi

Let $f$, $g\colon A\to B$ be two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms between two A$_{\infty}$-algebras (linear over a commutative ring $\mathbb{K}$). In this paper, we compare different notions of (right) homotopy between $f$ and $g$. We note that the A$_{\infty}$-algebra $B\otimes R$, where $R:=\mathbb{K}[t,dt]$, is a model for the interval $[0,1]\times B$ in the sense of Fukaya-Oh-Ohta-Ono, and we give a short alternative proof, in the unfiltered case, of the existence of comparison morphisms between such models. We use it to prove that two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms are homotopic \`a la Seidel if and only if, considered as morphisms of 2-colored DG operads, they are elementary homotopic \`a la Markl-Shnider-Stasheff through a homotopy which is constant on the two monochromatic parts. We also provide an example of two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms which are elementary homotopic but not weakly equivalent (and so homotopic \`a la Seidel). Moreover, over a field, we observe that the models for the interval are good path objects in the category of A$_{\infty}$-algebras with (non strict) A$_{\infty}$-morphisms, and we explain why weakly equivalent A$_{\infty}$-morphisms need not be homotopic.

entry.title: The first homology of square-section braid groups
entry.content:
Minh Pham, Nicholas Wawrykow, Jacob Zweiback

We compute the first homology of the unordered configuration space of $n$ open unit-squares in the $w$ by $h$ rectangle for all positive integers $n$, $w$, and $h$. Letting $w$ and $h$ vary, these square configuration spaces form a bi-filtration of the unordered configuration space of $n$ points in the plane, so their fundamental groups approximate the $n$-strand braid group. Using a pair of spectral sequences, we prove that these square and point configuration spaces have naturally isomorphic first homology groups if $w,h\ge 3$ and $n\le wh-3$. In the $h=2$ case, we show that the first homology groups of these square configuration spaces are free of rank $n-1$ for $n\le 2w-2$, whereas they are free of rank $w-1$ for $n=2w-1$.

entry.title: Weak and genuine A_n-formality for number fields
entry.content:
Ambrus P\'al, Gereon Quick

We introduce weak $A_n$-formality for Galois cochain algebras and, for profinite groups whose mod-$p$ cohomology is concentrated in degrees at most two, characterise weak and genuine $A_n$-formality through finite embedding problems and the projective system they form. We then study $A_n$-formality for number fields. Let $K$ be a number field and let $p$ be an odd prime with $\mu_p\not\subset K$. For $p\geq 5$, and for $p=3$ under a natural local cyclotomic condition, we prove that every associated finite $A_3$-embedding problem is solvable. In contrast, for every odd $p$ with $\mu_p\not\subset K$, we show that no compatible family of finite-stage solutions exists, and hence $C^\bullet(G_K,\mathbb F_p)$ is not genuinely $A_3$-formal. The proof uses Chebotarev density, governing fields, and the Gras-Munnier criterion to obstruct the compatibility of finite-stage solutions, and it builds on previous work of Maire-Min\'a\v{c}-Ramakrishna-T\^an. This shows that genuine $A_3$-formality detects a global compatibility obstruction for number fields invisible to every individual finite embedding problem and invisible to obstructions arising from individual strong Massey vanishing problems.

We develop a semisimple obstruction theory for finite-length abelian categories. To each object \(X\) we associate a canonical obstruction subobject \(\mathcal O(X)\), consisting of the part invisible to all morphisms into semisimple objects. The quotient \(X/\mathcal O(X)\) is semisimple and universal among such morphisms, yielding a canonical semisimplification reflector and characterizing semisimplicity by the vanishing of obstruction. Iterating the construction gives an obstruction filtration which, in finite-length module categories, recovers the classical radical filtration and Loewy theory. Obstruction is also heart-dependent: under Happel--Reiten--Smal{\o} tilting, extension data can appear as new obstruction layers, leading to obstruction shadows and visible torsion. Thus classical radical theory arises as the fixed-heart module-theoretic instance of a categorical framework for semisimple reconstruction, persistence, and variation of heart.

In this paper, we study the tensor triangular geometry of band algebras $RB$, where $B$ is a finite left regular band and $R$ is a commutative Noetherian ring. We show that the Balmer spectrum of $\Perf(RB)$ is homeomorphic to $\Spec R\times L_B$, where $L_B$ is the support lattice of $B$. We also show that there is a bijection between the localizing ideals of $D(RB)$ and the stable subsets of $\Spec R\times L_B$. As a consequence, the telescope conjecture holds for $D(RB)$. Finally, we construct a band $B$ such that the generalized Nerves of Steel Conjecture fails for the non-rigid tensor triangulated category $\Perf(RB)$.

For $n\ge1$, we study representations of a simplicial group $G$ in the full $\infty$-subcategory of simplicial vector spaces whose normalized homology is concentrated in degrees $0,\ldots,n-1$, retaining its full mapping spaces. The resulting functor category depends only on the $n$-truncated homotopy type of $\mathbf{B}G$ and admits projectively bifibrant strict diagram and simplicial group-algebra module models. If restriction along a specified map $f:G\to H$ is an equivalence, then $\pi_0(f)$ is a group isomorphism; the proof uses ordinary extension and restriction of scalars. Yet for every $n\ge2$ and prime $q$ invertible in $k$, the nontrivial source $K(\mathbb Z/q,n-1)$ has the same $n$-representation category with vertex evaluation as the trivial group. The group-algebra augmentation is a weak equivalence, so the constant functor is also an equivalence for untruncated representations. Thus $n$-representations depend only on the $n$-truncation of $\mathbf{B}G$, but need not determine that truncation, even together with vertex evaluation.

Multiparameter complex processes, based on the Costa-Farber model, provide a common framework for growing random simplicial complexes, including the Linial-Meshulam and random flag complex processes. We establish laws of large numbers for persistent Betti numbers of these processes and prove that, after a deterministic time change and normalization, their persistence diagrams converge weakly in probability to a deterministic finite measure. Its quadrant masses are determined by universal limits of normalized persistent Betti numbers, characterized by an explicit finite-dimensional optimization problem. We extend the diagram convergence to integrals of continuous functions with polynomial growth in the death coordinate and controlled singularities at the diagonal. These results yield convergence of additive and multiplicative lifetime measures and total persistence. We further deduce convergence in optimal transport distance. The proofs combine local weak convergence of simplicial pairs, spectral analysis of compressed Laplacians accounting for dependence through shared faces, and quantitative estimates for large death coordinates and short lifetimes.

We show that the origin is an isolated invariant set of $\varphi_f$ and that its Conley index is the suspension of the Milnor fiber, \[ h(\varphi_f,\{0\})\;\simeq\;\Sigma F_f\;\simeq\;\bigvee_{\mu(f)}S^n , \] so that $\mu(f)=\rank \CH_n(\varphi_f,\{0\};\Z)$: the Milnor number is the rank of the homological Conley index of the flow in degree $n$. Since $\im f$ is a first integral of the flow, after a rotation of the target through an angle avoiding finitely many values there are no connecting orbits between the $\mu(f)$ nondegenerate rest points that result, and the sum property of the Conley index applies. McCord's theorem then recovers the Poincar\'e--Hopf index of $-\nabla\re f$.

We first compute the complete local deformation ring of the invariant space of constants and squares in characteristic two, using six Grassmannian coordinates. For every Artinian specialization, evaluation at the identity has a finite free rank-four stabilizer. Its fourth-power morphism is $(x,y)\mapsto(2bxy,2axy)$, and its eighth-power morphism is trivial. This identifies $(2a,2b)$ as the common obstruction to fourth-power vanishing, normality of the stabilizer, and two-sidedness in an equivalent cyclic-module construction.

A direct $p$-adic expansion turns this degree bound into a uniform solution of the cusp relation modulo nilpotents. Consequently every ring $R$ admits a faithfully flat algebra with seminormal reduction, and every invertible $R[T]$-module becomes free after a faithfully flat extension of $R$, answering a question of Drinfeld.

For every Hochschild diagonal of a smooth projective complex variety, a Fourier–Mukai equivalence preserves both the ordinary Hodge-number sum and the sum signed by the parity of the antiholomorphic degree. In dimension five these invariants determine $h^{0,3}$ and $h^{1,4}$ and reduce the unrestricted Hodge-number problem to two numerical parameters, one of which is the possible failure of invariance of $h^{0,2}$. The general fivefold case remains open, while a theorem of Abuaf proves invariance of all Hodge numbers for fivefolds with trivial canonical bundle.

author.name: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz

entry.content:

We explain a Lean 4 formalization of the classical Seifert van Kampen theorem for the full fundamental groupoid. For an arbitrary topological space covered by two open subsets, the inclusion-induced square of ordinary continuous-path fundamental groupoids is a pushout in the category of categories. Every point is retained as an object; no basepoint, connectedness, or separation hypothesis is required. The development identifies an auxiliary directed path category for the indiscrete preorder with Mathlib's fundamental groupoid through strictly inverse functors and naturality equalities. It then assembles the pushout universal property from attributed path-subdivision and homotopy-grid helpers adapted from the directed-topology formalization of Basold, Bruin, and Lawson. We describe the descent construction, its transfer to ordinary fundamental groupoids, and the statement and verification boundaries of the exact artifact registered in Palomar. This is an expository account of a classical theorem and an existing formal artifact, with no claim of mathematical novelty or formalization priority.

entry.title: Collapsibility of Alexander duals for shade maps

Let $E$ be a nonempty finite set. A shade map on $E$ is a map $T:\mathcal{P}(E) ightarrow\mathcal{P}(E)$ such that toggling an element $u otin T(F)$ in the input $F$ does not change $T(F)$. We prove that, if $T$ is an inclusion-reversing shade map and $G\subseteq E$, then the simplicial complex \[ \{F\subseteq E\mid G\subseteq T(F)\} \] is collapsible. Equivalently, if $S$ is an inclusion-preserving shade map, then the Alexander dual of \[ \{F\subseteq E\mid G ot \subseteq S(F)\} \] is collapsible. This is an Alexander-dual companion to the shade-map collapsibility theorem in \emph{The Elser nuclei sum revisited}. The proof first matches all faces on which $T(F) eq E$ by a toggle. The remaining faces, characterized by $T(F)=E$, form the free convex set complex of an associated antimatroidal quasi-closure operator. We give a self-contained recursive acyclic matching on this complex. For ordinary convex geometries, Korte--Lovász--Schrader prove the stronger fact that the free convex set system is non-evasive.

A systematic way to construct Poisson brackets on moduli stacks in algebraic geometry is through shifted Poisson structures on derived stacks. The standard construction, due to Calaque--Pantev--To{\"e}n--Vaqui{\'e}--Vezzosi, imports Gelfand--Kazhdan formal geometry to derived stacks in order to establish formal descent for polyvector fields. The result is a graded Lie algebra which we call the ``crystalline'' polyvector fields on a derived stack. Using instead the formal derived geometry machinery of Gaitsgory--Rozenblyum, we construct a graded Lie algebra of ``infinitesimal'' polyvector fields which has a direct geometric interpretation: it governs deformations of the formal shifted cotangent stack, together with its canonical exact symplectic form. Our main result is an equivalence between crystalline and infinitesimal polyvector fields on a derived stack as graded Lie algebra objects, providing a deformation-theoretic perspective on the graded Lie algebra constructed by Calaque--Pantev--To{\"e}n--Vaqui{\'e}--Vezzosi.

entry.title: Pauli problem in dimension 4
entry.content:
Dmitry Grinko

The finite-dimensional Pauli problem asks how many measurements in orthonormal bases determine every pure state of a \(d\)-level quantum system up to a global phase. Four bases always suffice, and the answer is known to be three for \(d=2\) and four for \(d=3\) and \(d\geq5\). Dimension four remained open because the embedding argument used in other dimensions fails there: the pure-state space \(\mathbb{CP}^3\) embeds in \(\R^9\), the space of the nine independent probabilities of three bases. We show that three bases do not suffice in \(\C^4\), so exactly four are needed. The same argument shows that no ten vectors in \(\C^4\) do phase retrieval. Since eleven vectors are known to suffice, the smallest phase-retrieval frame and the smallest rank-one POVM distinguishing all pure states in \(\C^4\) both have eleven elements. All three lower bounds follow from one statement: every six-dimensional real space of traceless Hermitian \(4\times4\) matrices with a common isotropic vector, that is, a nonzero \(e\) with \(e^*Te=0\) for all \(T\) in the space, contains a nonzero matrix of rank at most two. We prove it with complex \(K\)-theory: otherwise, an odd unitary map on the five-sphere would have a \(K^1\)-class that is nonzero by antipodal symmetry but vanishes because of the isotropic vector.

The resulting radical-ideal classification implies the Hovey-Strickland classification of thick tensor ideals in the category of dualizable $K(n)$-local spectra via the forward implication of Barthel-Heard-Naumann. The special-fiber argument is local and geometric. After cutting an invariant prime by a one-parameter curve, we construct from the Cartier structure equation a smooth formal quotient $\mathcal{Q}$ and a distinguished subgroup $\mathcal{H}$. The generic fiber of $\mathcal{H}$ is identified with the deformation space of connected-\'etale extensions. $\mathbb{Z}_p$-folded surfaces are a class of oriented folded surfaces with a fundamental $H_2(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})$ class. In this paper we study the $\mathbb{Z}_p$-folded surfaces that embed in $3$-manifolds. This perspective naturally leads to the definition of the $\mathbb{Z}_p$-Thurston norm, which generalises the $\mathbb{Z}_2$-Thurston norm of Jaco, Rubinstein and Tillmann and adapts Turaev's definition of $\theta$. We define canonical $\mathbb{Z}_p$-folded surfaces, which connect the theory of $\mathbb{Z}_p$-folded surfaces to the study of one-vertex $3$-manifold triangulations, and we relate their Euler characteristic to the $\mathbb{Z}_p$-Thurston norm. We generalise a classical result of Bredon and Wood by proving that the maximum Euler characteristic of a non-separating non-empty $\mathbb{Z}_3$-folded surface embedded in $L(3n,1)$ is $2-n$ for $n\in\mathbb{Z}^{>0}$, determining the $\mathbb{Z}_3$-Thurston norm in these cases. We conclude by demonstrating the motivating application of this theory to the study of generalised triangulations by proving that any generalised triangulation of the lens space $L(3n,1)$ must have at least $n$ tetrahedra. This final result is a preview of joint work with Spreer in which we determine the exact complexity of $L(3n,1)$ using more sophisticated techniques.

The computational complexity of simplicial homology has been studied since the question was raised by Kaibel and Pfetsch, and clique homology was later shown to be $\mathsf{QMA}_1$-hard by Crichigno and Kohler. King and Kohler subsequently introduced the weighted, spectrally gapped version considered here and developed a reduction intended to establish the same hardness result in this setting. We give a complete proof of the hard direction. The earlier King-Kohler argument contains a gap in the analysis of the nontrivially folded local gadgets, so the required topological and spectral properties have to be re-established on the clique complexes actually produced by the reduction. This is not a local repair of the published proof: the argument requires a new analysis of the local topology, the filtered cochain complexes, and the interaction of many overlapping gadgets. Our proof uses exact finite certificates for the local combinatorial data and relative homology to determine the effect of each gadget on the encoded qubit space. We then prove the finite-dimensional filtered-Hodge statement needed to recover the corresponding rank-one low-energy penalty and derive a quantitative global estimate that transfers the source-Hamiltonian promise gap to the final weighted Hodge Laplacian. Consequently, for fixed efficiently computable $k(n)$ and inverse-polynomial $\gamma(n)$, weighted gapped clique homology is $\mathsf{QMA}_1(\mathcal G)$-hard. The previously known $\mathsf{QMA}$-containment argument is logically independent of the gap and remains unaffected.

entry.title: Scalable persistence pairing graphs on scalar fields with an application to porous media
entry.content:
John Rick Manzanares

We present a scalable method for computing persistence pairing graphs from large cubical filtrations and use it to test whether graph organization among persistent classes contains information beyond persistence intervals alone. The method cancels equal-value pairs before global reduction, constructs the compressed complex in streaming form, and recovers graph transitions from one persistence reduction through projected relations and triangular event solves. We apply the method to 119 signed distance volumes from the DRP-372 porous media collection for permeability prediction. Each 256-cubed volume induces more than 135 million cubical cells before contraction, whereas the median compressed complex contains 37,471 generators. In validation grouped by material family, adding persistence pairing graph descriptors improves prediction over persistence summaries under both Ridge regression and partial least squares regression. In the stricter experiment that holds out one source project at a time, Ridge retains a modest improvement over persistence alone, although additional benefit beyond geometry and persistence is not consistent across projects. Two null models show that the observed persistence and graph coupling and edge target organization are strongly nonrandom, but neither uniquely explains the predictive improvement; the useful signal appears to reside mainly in coarser graph and event organization. Spatial analyses likewise distinguish persistence magnitude from graph prominence and reveal nonlocal organization among algebraically related persistence events. These results show that persistence pairing graphs provide structurally informative summaries beyond the barcode while exposing domain dependence and representative sensitivity that motivate more invariant relational descriptors.
